from itertools import combinations
s='''9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9
9 9 9 9 1 9 9 9 9 1 9
9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9
9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 1 9 9
9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9

9 9 9 9 9 9 9 1 9 9 9
1 9 9 9 9 9 1 1 9 9 9'''
out='''9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9 9
9 9 9 9 1 3 3 3 3 1 9
9 9 9 9 3 9 9 9 9 3 9
9 9 9 9 3 9 9 9 1 3 9
9 9 9 9 3 9 9 9 9 3 9
1 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 1 9
3 9 9 9 3 9 9 9 9 9 9
3 9 9 1 1 9 9 9 9 9 9
3 9 9 9 9 9 9 1 9 9 9
1 3 3 3 3 3 1 1 9 9 9'''
g=[list(map(int,r.split())) for r in s.splitlines()]; o=[list(map(int,r.split())) for r in out.splitlines()]
p=[(r,c) for r in range(10) for c in range(11) if g[r][c]==1]
for (r,c),(u,v) in combinations(p,2):
 dr=u-r;dc=v-c
 if dr==0 or dc==0 or abs(dr)==abs(dc):
  n=max(abs(dr),abs(dc)); sr=(dr>0)-(dr<0);sc=(dc>0)-(dc<0)
  cells=[(r+sr*k,c+sc*k) for k in range(1,n)]
  if cells and all(o[x][y]==3 for x,y in cells): print('ok', (r,c),(u,v),cells)
  elif any(o[x][y]==3 for x,y in cells): print('partial', (r,c),(u,v),[(x,y,o[x][y]) for x,y in cells])

name: arc-align-markers
description: Use when an ARC grid has sparse marker cells and demonstrations show straight colored links. Connect markers only along shared rows or columns.

# ARC: connect aligned markers

Use this rule when examples show a sparse background (often color 1), marker cells (often color 7), and a new line color (often color 3).

1. Preserve all original marker cells and all unrelated background cells.
2. In each row, find marker cells and fill every cell strictly between consecutive markers with the demonstrated line color.
3. Do the same in each column, filling only the cells strictly between consecutive markers.
4. Do not draw diagonals, extend links beyond endpoints, or connect non-aligned markers.
5. When row and column links intersect, the shared cell remains the line color.
6. Return the grid at its original dimensions.

Validate the rule against a demonstration before applying it: compare proposed changed cells with the output, especially whether links are axis-aligned and whether only intervening cells are filled.
